newsitem.title: USA: Inactive Anchor Glass unit files for Chapter 11.
newsitem.headline: Inactive Anchor Glass unit files for Chapter 11.

text.p: An inactive unit of Vitro SA's Anchor Glass Container Corp has joined the parent company in filing for Chapter 11 protection in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, according to court papers.

The unit, Anchor Recycling Corp, a former general partner that recycled waste glass, listed assets of $2 million and off-balance sheet liabilities of about $20 million owed to Anchor Glass Container Corp employee pension funds.
Anchor Glass Container Corp filed for Chapter 11 protection on September 13 and in court papers listed assets of $1.2 billion and liabilities of $951.1 million.
Vitro reached a non-binding agreement on September 13 with Ball-Foster Container Co to sell Anchor's assets for an estimated $365 million.
Anchor is the third-largest U.S. glass container company.
Ball-Foster is 42 percent owned by Indiana-based container company Ball Corp and 58 percent owned by French glass container company Compagnie de Saint-Gobain.
